reviews.text:
I was looking for options to get some tests done for my dog ​​and I read very good reviews of the KENVELO clinic, so I decided to go there.

I was completely satisfied with the care provided by the team of doctors. I felt calm and cared for, but above all, my dog ​​Coco was treated with so much love.

I am incredibly grateful to all the doctors at KENVELO for the care they gave me and my dog.

Dangerous for pets, this is your typical vet clinic where they're just looking to squeeze more money out of you with unnecessary tests, leaving the animals in the same or worse condition. I absolutely do not recommend it, unless you want to throw your money away and put your pet at risk. Don't go there, for your own good. If you want to save your pet or receive efficient, quality service, go to the San Francisco Veterinary Hospital, located near Fidel Velasquez and Alcalde. They are good there and their prices are fair. They saved my dog ​​from a terminal illness. It's in a different area, but it's worth it.

I live far away, and whenever I need something for my pets, I go there. Dr. Ivan is very well-prepared (internal medicine, oncology, and whenever I see him, he's studying something new). He saved my rabbit, Licho, who was quite old and had an intestinal obstruction. He also helped us with a dog a year and a half ago who had very advanced breast cancer, but we had a beautiful farewell (they played music, lit candles, and everything was very family-oriented). I always recommend him to anyone who asks. The vet who works with him is incredibly kind to our dogs and is also very knowledgeable.

They provide excellent service, are efficient in responding, and are very kind. I wish I had known about this place before my pet died (other places had misdiagnoses and a lack of experience). A very good place, 100% recommended.
Always very attentive and with feline specialists. Convenient hours.

Highly recommend! I took my guinea pig there for a checkup because another veterinary clinic had given us a very bad diagnosis. I sought a second opinion and found the right place. The treatment my pet received was excellent, and the doctor was very kind. Thank you, Kenvelo Clinic!

VERY BAD EXPERIENCE. A few weeks ago, I took my cat to the vet because he had a broken leg. I called before arriving to see if they could treat him, and the woman said yes. It was a Saturday at 1 a.m., and it was clear that the person was having trouble even shaving his paw. Because of the urgency, I trusted everything she said and did. She applied a lot of things, including anesthesia, which wasn't intravenous but intramuscular. Since then, my cat has completely changed. Before that, my kitten was healthy and strong.

She told me I could go home with my kitten and that he would be fine within the next two hours. My cat didn't fully wake up, so I decided to return the next day. It was a different shift and different staff. The veterinarian on duty barely examined him, and the two people assisting him started administering more medications. My cat stopped breathing and died there. I don't recommend it. They don't provide proper care; they left him alone, and now I'm suffering one of the worst experiences of my life. If it's an emergency, please avoid it.

0 stars, very bad service. They treated me rudely and were very disrespectful. Even though you pay them, they make faces at you and throw your money at you. Not recommended. Another veterinary clinic is better.

Today, October 2, 2025, I took my dog ​​to this place because we noticed a strange swelling on her right hind leg, thinking it might be from an animal bite. To begin with, they took a very long time to attend to us, even though there was more than one person in the clinic and it was an emergency. They asked us to leave her for 12 hours to monitor her and reduce the swelling, and that's when the problems started.

Three hours after we brought her in, they sent us a picture showing her back leg shaved and a hematoma with swelling. Naturally, I asked what they meant by the hematoma and if they had found the cause, but they couldn't give me a clear answer. Later, they asked us to authorize an X-ray, which, in my opinion, was unnecessary since they had already ruled out the possibility of the swelling being due to trauma. However, we agreed to have it done. They also mentioned that they were going to puncture the area to take a sample. After several hours, they told us that a significant number of neutrophils were present, but that she was stable. At that point, they asked if they could feed her, which we agreed to. The next message they sent us is what started to alarm us, because they asked us to authorize her staying longer in the hospital for further monitoring. When I asked why this was necessary, they replied almost two hours later, only to tell me it was to control her fever and continue monitoring the inflammation. Since nothing particularly serious was mentioned, we decided that the best thing would be to care for her at home.

When we arrived at the clinic, there was only one person working, and it took them an hour to release our dog to us. Before they gave her to us, I asked if she had improved at all, and the person at the clinic said yes, the swelling had gone down. But when she finally came to us, her wound was THREE TIMES WORSE. The swelling had increased in size and spread from just her paw to her entire leg. We were obviously shocked because she hadn't been like that before, and as we were about to leave, I mentioned to the person in charge that I didn't think it was right that her paw was worse than when she arrived. As soon as I said that, the person started messaging the doctor to find out what was happening. Then they told us that if we took the dog out of the clinic, we would have to sign a release form stating that if anything happened to her, they wouldn't be responsible. At that moment, we refused to sign the release because my dog ​​was under their care, and yet she ended up worse than when she arrived. The person in charge immediately told us the doctor would call if we wanted an explanation. We agreed, and he started telling us things that were NEVER mentioned in the messages: that the bite had a lot of pus inside the muscle and that they had been draining the wound all day, which is why they wanted to monitor her longer. He said that if we wanted her to leave, we needed to sign a release form, essentially absolving them of any responsibility for anything that might happen afterward. We explained that they had never mentioned any of that and that we had even read the messages they had sent us. He said he didn't know when communication had been lost, which clearly happened when they took two hours to reply to messages. An argument ensued, which quickly escalated. He ended up telling us they couldn't keep the dog and that we were free to take her. We remained firm in our refusal to sign anything and simply left the clinic and took her with us. We're at another hospital now, and they're telling us that part of the wound was caused by the veterinarians themselves when they shaved his paw. Please be aware of this before entrusting your pets to these people.
I had an emergency with two of my hamsters and this clinic has been excellent for my little ones. The staff provides wonderful care and treat the animals with love and respect. I highly recommend it!
We arrived in an emergency and they attended to us very quickly, from 1 am until 4 am. Very professional ✨

I went to the emergency room and unfortunately there was only one person there. She was nice, but she couldn't help my pet alone. She tried many times to draw blood and only hurt him without getting any samples. I think there should be at least two people so they can support each other in any emergency. I had to go somewhere else with my pet, but I took him home already injured.
We have been taking our dogs to Dr. Ivan for a long time, and they have always given us excellent care and follow-up when required, as well as the attention of the clinic staff.

I chose this clinic because it's one of the few places in the city with a veterinarian specializing in exotic species. I took my red-eared slider in for wounds and swelling on its front legs, which turned out to be cat bites. My experience has been excellent. From reception to the consultation, the staff has been very friendly, professional, and attentive. It's a reputable clinic; I had to sign a consent form before they administered anesthesia and performed the necessary procedures. After the consultations, they send me follow-up messages to monitor my turtle's progress. They also provided me with written instructions on treatment and home care, which is very helpful for my memory problems. I definitely recommend this clinic if you have exotic pets.
